stories.headline: Tunsil's Arm Gives Out in Washington and Jayden Daniels Just Lost His Fence
stories.read: Laremy Tunsil tore a triceps clean through at Saturday's practice, he's under the knife, and Dan Quinn admits the big fella misses a serious chunk of the season. Andrew Wylie slides over to guard the blind side, and pardner, that ain't the same wall. Jayden Daniels already had trouble stayin' upright last year, and now the fellas chasin' him get a shorter ride to the quarterback, which means fewer of those long developin' routes Terry McLaurin makes his livin' on. Doc ain't tellin' you to sell Daniels, he's still a rare bird who runs for paydirt. But if you were reachin' for McLaurin a round early on deep-shot dreams, cool your heels and let somebody else pay that toll.

stories.headline: Alec Pierce Is Still Ridin' the Stationary Bike on a Hundred-Fourteen-Million-Dollar Saddle
stories.read: The Colts handed Pierce four years and a hundred and fourteen million this spring, and the man has not run a single route all summer. He's at every practice, all right, pedalin' a bike to nowhere and watchin' from the rail while that left ankle mends. Indy still swears he'll be saddled up Week 1 against Baltimore, but there's no date on the paper and the saloon is gettin' twitchy. Here's Doc's read: an outfit does not pay a fella that kind of money to be a decoy, so the throws are comin' when he's right. Let the nervous folks pass on him three rounds too early, then stake your claim and collect.

stories.headline: New England Pays Hunter Henry to Stay, and the Tight End Line Just Got Locked Shut
stories.read: Patriots handed the thirty-one-year-old two more years, sixteen million with a chance at twenty, fourteen and a half of it guaranteed. That's not retirement money, that's starter money. Henry caught sixty balls for seven scores last season, which was the most trips to paydirt on the whole ranch. Nobody behind him in that tight end room is takin' the job now, so quit wastin' a late pick on the young fella hopin' for a shakeup. Henry's a boring, steady wagon at the back end of the tight end pack, and boring wins more pots than pretty does.
